title: Metal shader baker - exports with `min_macos_version_arm64` < 14.00 abort on startup (Apple Silicon)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2 (this is the version I am speaking about in this report)
- Reproducible also in 4.7.0
- NOT reproducible in 4.6.3 - it works as expected (doesn't crash)

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.6.2) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 48.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When the macOS export preset has Shader Baker enabled and **`application/min_macos_version_arm64` is set below 14** (the default is 13 in 4.7.2, 11 in 4.7.0), the exported app aborts on startup before displaying a window.

Setting `min_macos_version_arm64` to `14.00` and re-baking produces a working build with zero errors.

This reproduces on a brand-new project containing one CSG cube, one light, one WorldEnvironment node with some settings enabled, one camera, with no custom shader code.

Additionally, there may be a clue in the output log when building, I am seeing the following when building against minimum 13 in Godot 4.7.2:

### Steps to reproduce

Requires an Apple Silicon Mac...

1. Open the attached MRP in Godot 4.7.2
2. Open up "Project > Export" and leave all the defaults. Ensure that Shader Baker is turned on
3. Ensure `application/min_macos_version_arm64` is **13.00**.
4. Delete `.godot/exported` from the project directory if it exists to ensure you're not reusing shader baker cache
5. Export a release build
6. Open the DMG and run the new app. It should crash
7. Now set `application/min_macos_version_arm64` in the project to **14.00**, delete `.godot/exported` again, re-export, and run. It should not crash
